data.why: the repo's own example_images are small, varied (an illustration of many discrete objects good for point/box annotation, and a photo) and the browser can upload them directly; seed/index.html replaces the repo's root index.html with the webkitdirectory-only folder input swapped for a plain multi-file input so the browser can supply files without a native directory picker

goals: import a set of images for a detection/segmentation dataset and confirm all of them loaded
draw a bounding box around every object of interest in an image to build a detection training set
place positive and negative points on an object to produce weak supervision masks for segmentation
pan and zoom into an image to place precise annotations on small or crowded objects
add a free-text description to an individual annotation to record its class or notes
save all annotations to JSON, reload the file later, and confirm each image kept its own annotations while navigating with Next/Previous

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately (local, browser-only box and point annotation of an image set, exported as one JSON file keyed by filename), its depth is right, and 7 of the 8 screens I opened show what their nodes claim; the eighth, 026, doesn't show the alert it is cited for. It should be filed after small fixes: reframe the reload task, record the A/D-while-typing and Undo-removes-description bugs, and add the missing mask-overlay feature.
